page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.3xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 12 vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 24.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. This instance operates on a KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data.

Performance benchmarks place this instance consistently in the average tier across multiple workloads. The single-core stress-ng score is 1579.29, while the multi-core score reaches 12489.46. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 699.05 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 70.8 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In data processing tasks, the instance achieves a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 27.2 GB/sec and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 59.03 GB/sec.

The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, which assist in vector calculations and deep learning inference. For small language models, prompt processing reaches 773.56 tokens/sec. However, performance drops to a weak rating of 17.92 tokens/sec for prompt processing on medium 7B models, highlighting a tradeoff when running larger models without dedicated GPU acceleration. Network performance is constrained to a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Given its dedicated compute resources and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.hfc7.3xlarge offers a balanced cost-to-performance profile for compute-intensive tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. It is well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, Redis-based caching, and moderate computational tasks.
